passage: Lunch and dinner tables across Peru often carry a bowl of sopa criolla.
Peruvians treat it as comfort food, and many households keep it in steady rotation.
The name translates as "creole soup," and creole points to local people who usually descend from European conquerors.
That single word hints at something larger about the country's cooking.
Peruvian cuisine has been shaped not just by indigenous ethnic groups but also by settlers who arrived from abroad.
The soup itself begins with thin noodles that cooks often call "angel hair."
Those noodles are boiled and ladled into a bowl of beef stock seasoned with garlic, onions, tomato paste, and milk.
A fried egg is set on top, which makes the dish look and taste delicious to Peruvians of every age.
choices: the difficulty of finding thin noodles in South American markets
the nutritional advantages of adding eggs to soup
how a familiar Peruvian soup reflects the mixed origins of the country's cuisine
the history of European conquest in South America

theme.explanation_ko: creole 이라는 이름의 뜻에서 출발해 페루 요리가 토착 집단과 외래 정착민 양쪽에 의해 형성되었다는 점을 짚고, 그 소박한 재료와 조리로 마무리하므로 ③가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 면을 구하기 어렵다는 언급이 없다. ② 달걀은 고명으로만 나오고 영양을 말하지 않는다. ④ 정복의 역사는 creole 의 뜻풀이로만 스친다. ⑤ 다른 점심 메뉴와 비교하지 않는다.
